- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion is evident in 30d forecasts: model often fails to capture gradual pullback after sharp rises; add a mild downward bias in the 10-15 day horizon.
- Forecasts for the first 5-7 days of the 30d window are often too optimistic; reduce initial values by 1-2% relative to recent 7-day average.
- If sentiment shows a sharp reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1-2 days ahead of true sentiment shift.
